messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

We need to simulate this system. There is a lot to process: we have an initial stock of 12 at start (time 0?). Need to reconstruct historical events up to target_time (100) based on eligible_events, applying only those events that have visible revisions before knowledge_cutoff (which equals target_time = 100). Actually knowledge_cutoff is 100. There's also note: "first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff." So we need to filter eligible_events to those where received_time <= 100. Then for each event_id, choose the highest visible revision (i.e., among those filtered events, choose max revision per event_id). Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time (100). Then apply these events in order (event_time, event_id) from initial_stock. That yields historical reconstruction up to target_time. Then compute stock_at_target (stock after processing events up to target_time). Also compute total historical_lost through target_time: sum of unmet demand amounts for historical events (i.e., demands where quantity > current stock at that moment; unmet portion = quantity - stock; but stock becomes zero after satisfying up to available). Note: A stockout is defined as strictly positive unmet demand, i.e., demand where quantity > stock, not just demand that leaves stock zero after exact consumption. So record lost quantity only for demands > stock (unmet quantity), and count as lost or lost sales. Also need first_future_stockout_time: earliest event_time in future_schedule (starting at 101 onward) that has unmet demand (i.e., demand quantity > stock at that moment). The future schedule also includes demands quantity zero, meaning no demand; receipts add stock. Also need future_lost: lost quantity for future events only (i.e., sum of unmet unmet demand? Actually lost for the scenario only: sum of lost quantity due to future schedule events; does not include historical lost). And stock_at_horizon: after processing all events up to horizon_time = 130. The horizon includes future events up to or beyond horizon_time? The schedule contains events up to event_time=118. Wait horizon_time is 130 (greater than all future schedule events times). There are no additional events beyond 118. So effectively after processing all future events, we end at time 118 but horizon_time is 130. There is no further events; so stock remains same up to 130.

We need to compute stock after processing all events (historical + future). Since future events happen after target_time (101,...118). Also note that we must apply future events starting from reconstructed stock at target_time (the stock after historical events). Also note that they say "After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario..." So just continue simulation with future_schedule events. Then compute stock after horizon_time (i.e., after processing all future events). Also compute future_lost (total lost quantity from demands in future_schedule only). Also find first future stockout time.

Now we need to implement this simulation. Need to pay attention to correct processing ordering of events (event_time, event_id). Note that each event has a unique event_id string. Sorting by event_time then event_id lexicographically presumably yields deterministic order. So we need to sort events accordingly.

Also need to verify that events in eligible_events may have multiple revisions. For each event_id, we should keep highest revision among those whose received_time <= knowledge_cutoff.

We need to process only events with event_time <= target_time (100). So any events after 100 are ignored for historical reconstruction.
